posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
I agree with all your points. However those are valid statements but not valid assertions to demand for extra extensions.

The grading document which is made available each term before course registration clearly states the course expectations from the students. The students have the flexibility to choose the number of courses and which courses to register for each course after assessing the course load and difficulty.

The BPT questions have had one week time duration mentioned explicitly in the grading document. Further, the deadline is set as one week keeping in mind the wide variation in student ability and performance. BPT questions are easily solvable in one week’s time even if you give 15-20 minutes a day.

Finally, a course can moderate its deadlines and rigor based on the student performance distribution, but only to some extent to maintain the expected level of rigor and integrity from the course. The extremas of a distribution are never used as litmus test for the course, rather its first and second moments are considered.

Finally, this message does not mean that there might not be any extensions. If there are any system issues, or any other unforeseen issues, or on the discretion of the course team, they might or might not provide an extension for the benefit of all.

Regards,
Sayan
